html:
Roi Mata was a paramount chief of central Vanuatu who died around 1600 and was buried on the islet of Retoka (Hat Island), off Efate, with dozens of followers.

Stories of him, told for centuries, say he brought peace between warring clans and set up a system of chiefly titles that still exists. In 1967 the archaeologist José Garanger dug at Retoka and found a mass burial matching the oral account.

His residence, death place and grave became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2008, the first in Vanuatu. Local people still keep the sites tabu. Compare the chiefly sites of Tonga and the Lapita graves at Teouma.
sum: Roi Mata was a paramount chief of central Vanuatu who died around 1600 and was buried on the islet of Retoka (Hat Island), off Efate, with dozens of followers.
